write.desc: This topic builds the Riemann integral of a bounded function on [a,b] from partitions and upper and lower Darboux sums, defines integrability as equality of the upper and lower integrals, and proves the Riemann criterion. These points belong together because each step uses the one before it, and they end in the working tool that every later proof about the integral uses.

points.name: Partitions and refinements of [a,b]
points.what: Know what a partition of [a,b] is (a finite ordered set of points a = x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_n = b), its subintervals and their lengths, what it means for one partition to refine another, and how to form the common refinement of two partitions as their union.

points.name: Upper and lower Darboux sums
points.what: For a bounded f on [a,b] and a partition P, define m_k and M_k as the infimum and supremum of f on each subinterval, form L(f,P) and U(f,P), and see that L(f,P) <= U(f,P) for the same partition. Be able to explain why boundedness is needed for these sums to exist.
outside: supremum and infimum of a bounded set of real numbers and the completeness axiom guaranteeing they exist

points.name: Refining a partition raises lower sums and lowers upper sums
points.what: Prove that if Q refines P then L(f,P) <= L(f,Q) <= U(f,Q) <= U(f,P), by adding one point at a time and comparing the infimum and supremum over a subinterval with those over its two pieces.
outside: the supremum of a subset is at most the supremum of the whole set, and the infimum of a subset is at least the infimum of the whole set

points.name: Every lower sum is at most every upper sum
points.what: Prove that L(f,P) <= U(f,Q) for any two partitions P and Q, by passing to their common refinement and using the refinement lemma.

points.name: Upper and lower integrals
points.what: Define the upper integral as the infimum of all upper sums and the lower integral as the supremum of all lower sums, show that both exist, and prove that the lower integral is at most the upper integral.
outside: if every element of a set A is at most every element of a set B, then sup A <= inf B

points.name: Definition of Riemann integrability
points.what: Define f as Riemann integrable on [a,b] when its upper and lower integrals are equal, with the integral as the common value. Understand that the integral is a supremum and an infimum at once, and that integrability is a property that has to be proved.

points.name: Integrating constant and step functions from the definition
points.what: Compute the integral of a constant function and of a step function with one jump directly from upper and lower sums, choosing partitions that put the jump inside a short subinterval and computing the upper and lower integrals as an infimum and a supremum.

points.name: Integrating x and x^2 on [0,1] from the definition
points.what: Use the uniform partition into n pieces to compute U and L for f(x) = x and f(x) = x^2 on [0,1] exactly, and show that the upper and lower integrals are both 1/2 and 1/3 by taking an infimum and a supremum over n.
outside: closed formulas for 1 + 2 + ... + n and 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2
the Archimedean property (1/n can be made smaller than any positive number)

points.name: The Dirichlet function is not integrable
points.what: Show that the function equal to 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals has every lower sum equal to 0 and every upper sum equal to 1 on [0,1], so its lower and upper integrals differ. This shows a bounded function need not be integrable.
outside: density of the rationals and of the irrationals in the real numbers

points.name: The Riemann criterion for integrability
points.what: State and prove both directions of the criterion: a bounded f is integrable on [a,b] if and only if for every epsilon > 0 there is a partition P with U(f,P) - L(f,P) < epsilon. Each direction uses the epsilon characterisation of the supremum and infimum, together with the refinement lemma.
outside: epsilon characterisation of supremum and infimum (for every epsilon > 0 some element of the set lies within epsilon of the sup or inf)

points.name: Using the Riemann criterion in practice
points.what: Use the criterion to prove that a function is integrable without first finding the integral: estimate U(f,P) - L(f,P) as a sum of oscillation times length and choose P so it falls below epsilon. Use the sequence form (integrable exactly when some sequence of partitions has U - L tending to 0, and then the integral is the common limit of U and L), and recognise non-integrability through the negated criterion.
outside: limits of sequences of real numbers and the squeeze theorem

points.name: Riemann sums with tags and the mesh definition
points.what: Know the tagged Riemann sum, which picks one point in each subinterval, and the mesh of a partition. See that every tagged sum lies between L(f,P) and U(f,P), and know, without the proof, that defining the integral as the limit of tagged sums as the mesh goes to 0 gives the same integrable functions and the same integral.
